summary: Full read of 13 SEC whistleblower award orders (June 2023 - April 2024), the SEC combined award/denial order file of March 2023 (Release 97202), SEC press release 2023-89, a Senate PSI opening statement on Boeing, three TIGTA audits of the IRS Whistleblower Office (2009, 2016, 2023) and the Treasury KARRP page. SEC orders: 5 new denial case rows, 1 case row (the $114 million record mentioned in the 2023 press release), 2 events (SEC vacates its own denial on remand; refusal to exceed the 30% cap or pay on bankruptcy recoveries), and suggested corrections (including the missing approximately $1.5 million amount in Release 98235). TIGTA audits: 452 observations (claim intake, closures by reason, staffing, processing times, award rates, AIMS assessment results, TFA notices), rules and events; 5 proposed indicators (amounts_alleged, whistleblowers_filing, claims_processed_step, exam_assessment_per_hour, exam_no_change_rate) and 2 proposed rule names (notification_deadline_days, status_requests_per_year).

events.title: SEC vacates its own award denial after a voluntary remand from the Fifth Circuit
events.description: After a denied claimant petitioned the Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit, the SEC sought a voluntary remand, vacated its December 2, 2022 order (Release No. 96439), found the claimant was a whistleblower in his personal capacity, waived his late Form TCR under Section 36(a), and granted him an award; it warned that outside the Form TCR context extraordinary circumstances are still required.

events.title: SEC refuses to pay awards on what it could have collected, on bankruptcy recoveries, or above the 30% cap
events.description: In an award order the Commission held that awards are based on sanctions actually collected, not on amounts it was able to collect, that recoveries in bankruptcy proceedings are not monetary sanctions in a covered or related action, and that it will not use its Section 36(a) exemptive authority to pay more than the statutory 30% maximum.
events.quote: we have never used our discretion under Section 36(a)(1) of the Exchange Act to exempt a whistleblower from a statutory requirement or to approve an award amount above the statutory limit.

events.title: IRS Whistleblower Office starts using the E-TRAK claim inventory system
events.description: The initial release of E-TRAK, meant to replace three separate claim-tracking systems (ICEWEB, I-TRAK and an Access database), came into use in January 2009; reporting capabilities were in place by 30 June 2009.
events.quote: The initial release of the system that management has been developing since the standup of the Whistleblower Office was brought into use in January 2009.

events.title: Whistleblower Office creates a Strategic Planning and Program Administration unit
events.description: The SPPA unit (budget, policy, staffing, planning, congressional liaison) was developed in December 2010, part of the growth of the office from 20 employees in FY2011 to 61 in FY2015.
events.quote: Significant organization and staffing changes included development of the SPPA unit in December 2010

events.title: Whistleblower Office creates an Award Recommendation and Coordination unit
events.description: The ARC unit, handling litigation support and award determinations, was developed in June 2013; ICE and ARC staffing roughly doubled in FY2015.
events.quote: development of the ARC unit in June 2013, and approximately doubling the staffing for the ICE and ARC units in FY 2015.

events.title: IRS rejection and denial letters start giving reasons; preliminary 7623(b) denials with 30-day comment period
events.description: From October 2014 letters rejecting 7623(a) and (b) claims and denying 7623(b) claims state the basis, and 7623(b) denials get a preliminary letter and a 30-day review and comment period; 7623(a) preliminary award notification followed in December 2014.
events.quote: For § 7623(b) denials prior to October 2014, the WO letter to whistleblowers did not provide the basis for denial.

events.title: IRS moves preliminary award communications earlier
events.description: From 1 August 2016 the Whistleblower Office sends the preliminary award recommendation package right after full proceeds are collected, which it says can start the exchange with whistleblowers almost 24 months earlier.
events.quote: we are moving up the date of our communications with whistleblowers on the preliminary award recommendation package to right after full proceeds from an action have been collected

events.title: IRS Whistleblower Office starts recording the type of allegation on each claim
events.description: A claim-issue field added to e-Trak in FY2021 began to be completed in June 2021, letting the office report the most common allegations (unreported income first) in its FY2021 annual report.
events.quote: In June 2021, the Whistleblower Office started completing the claim issue field to compile data on e-Trak pertaining to the type of allegations submitted on Form 211.

events.title: IRS issues its FY2021 whistleblower annual report more than eight months late
events.description: The Whistleblower Office issued its FY2021 Annual Report to Congress on 10 June 2022, although GAO had recommended issuing it by 31 January; the clearance process and a change of director delayed it.
events.quote: the Whistleblower Office did not issue the Whistleblower Office Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2021 until June 10, 2022.
